title: Proposition
body_md: Let $Y^{\mathrm{mat}} \subseteq (\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}$ be a matroid Schubert variety and let $Y_L \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{2^n-1}$ be its image in the Segre embedding. Then $I(Y_L)$ is generated in degree $2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In \cite{ardila2016closure} the multihomogeneous ideal of the matroid Schubert varieties in the multigraded coordinate ring of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}$ is given in terms of the circuits of the matroid: let $J_{\mathrm{circuit}} \subseteq \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]$ be this ideal. Here $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]$ denotes the homogeneous coordinate ring of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}$, that is a polynomial ring in $2n$ variables with a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-multigrading. The generators of $J_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ are multilinear: their degree in the multigrading of $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]$ is a vector of $0$'s and $1$'s. Let $N := 2^n-1$ and let $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{P}^N]$ be the homogeneous coordinate ring of the ambient space of the Segre embedding of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}$. Let $I_\mathrm{Seg}$ be the ideal of the Segre variety, which is generated by quadrics. 

    The Segre embedding $(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n} \to \mathbb{P}^N$ defines an isomorphism $S / I_\mathrm{Seg} \to \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{\mathbb{Z}(1  , \dots ,  1)}$, where $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{\mathbb{Z}(1  , \dots ,  1)} = \bigoplus_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{(m  , \dots ,  m)}$ is the \emph{diagonal subalgebra} of $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]$. By construction, $I(Y_L) / I_\mathrm{Seg}$ is the preimage of $J_{\mathrm{circuit}} \cap \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{\mathbb{Z}(1  , \dots ,  1)}$.

    Given a multilinear generator $f \in J_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ of degree $\mathbf{e} \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, consider the $(2^{n- |\mathbf{e}|})$-dimensional subspace $f \cdot \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{(1  , \dots ,  1) - \mathbf{e}} \subseteq J_{\mathrm{circuit}} \cap \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{(1  , \dots ,  1)}$. It is easy to prove that $J_{\mathrm{circuit}} \cap \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\times n}]_{\mathbb{Z}(1  , \dots ,  1)}$ is generated by all elements constructed in this way. Since they have multidegree $(1  , \dots ,  1)$, these equations all pullback in $S / I_\mathrm{Seg}$ to linear equations. This shows $I(Y_L) = I_\mathrm{Seg} + (I(Y_L)_1)$, thus it is generated in degree $2$.

label: example: counterexample quadratic ideal
title: Example
body_md:
\label{example: counterexample quadratic ideal}
Let $\dim V = \dim W = 4$ and let $L \subseteq V^* \otimes W$ be a general $7$-dimensional linear space. We show that $Y_L \subseteq \mathrm{Gr}(4, V \oplus W)$ is not set-theoretically cut out by quadrics. To see this, we determine a linear subspace $\Sigma \subseteq \mathbb{P} \smash{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{\scalerel*{\bigwedge}{\Lambda}}}}^4( V \oplus W)$ such that $Y_L \cap \Sigma$ is a cubic surface contained in a $\mathbb{P}^3$: if $Y_L$ was cut out by quadrics, then its linear sections would be cut out by quadrics as well, yielding a contradiction. 

The linear space $\Sigma$ is described by a Schubert condition on $\mathrm{Gr}(4, V \oplus W)$. Let $U \subseteq W$ be a general $3$-dimensional subspace and let $\Sigma_U = \{ [E] \in \mathrm{Gr}(4, V \oplus W) : U \subseteq E \subseteq U \oplus V\}$. This is a classical Schubert variety whose associated partition is $(4,4,4,1)$: in particular, it defines a $\mathbb{P}^3 \subseteq \mathrm{Gr}(4, V \oplus W)$ parameterised by $\mathbb{P} V \to \Sigma_U$ sending $v \mapsto U \oplus \langle v \rangle$. 

We prove that $Y_L \cap \Sigma_U$ is a cubic surface. First, we show $Y_L \cap \Sigma_U$ contains a cubic surface. Set $L_U = L \cap (V^* \otimes U)$: by genericity $\dim L_U = 3$. For every $A \in L_U$, we have $\mathrm{rank} A \leq 3$: if equality holds, then $\lim_{t \to \infty} \Gamma_{tA} = U \oplus \ker A \in Y_L \cap \Sigma_U$ as in \Cref{prop: im plus ker}. This parameterises a surface 
\[
S_U := \overline{ \{ U \oplus \ker A : A \in L, \mathrm{im} A = U\} }\subseteq Y_L \cap \Sigma_U . \]
Observe that $\deg S_U = 3$ in the Pl\"ucker embedding of $\mathrm{Gr}(4,V \oplus W)$: for a fixed basis $A_1,A_2,A_3$ of $L_U$, the surface $S_U$ is parameterised by $v\in \mathbb{P} V$ such that $A_1v,A_2v,A_3v$ are linearly dependent elements of $U$. Since $\dim L_U = \dim U = 3$, this is equivalent to the vanishing of a $3 \times 3$ determinant. This shows $S_U \subseteq Y_L \cap \Sigma_U$.

For the inclusion $Y_L \cap \Sigma_U \subseteq S_U$, consider $[E] \in Y_L \cap \Sigma_U$ and write $E = U \oplus \langle v \rangle$. Since $[E] \in Y_L$, there is a curve $A(t)$ in $L$ with $E = \lim_{t \to \infty} \Gamma_{A(t)}$. Let $[0:A_0] \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{C} \oplus L)$ be the limit point $[0:A_0] = \lim_{t \to \infty} [1 : A(t)]$. Therefore, $A(t) = t^k A_0 +  o(t^{k})$; since $A(t) \in L$, we have $A_0 \in L$ as well. The same calculation as above shows $\mathrm{im} A_0 \subseteq U$ and $v \in \ker A_0$. This shows $E = U \oplus \ker A_0$, so $[E] \in S_U$ and $\operatorname{\mathnormal{Y_L}} \cap \Sigma_U=S_U$.
